docs.title: FiveM Loading Screen
docs.text:
A polished, fully customizable loading screen for FiveM servers: your name and colors, video or image backgrounds, music, rules, team, gallery, social links and a keybind overlay. Free to download.

You do not need to edit any code or JSON. Design it in your browser with a live preview, then download a ready-to-run resource.

  • Video backgrounds (local WEBM or MP4, or YouTube) with an animated image fallback
  • Music playback with skip, progress and volume controls
  • A keyboard overlay with your own keybind tooltips
  • Animated title presets, rules, team, gallery and custom panels
  • 12 languages, with right-to-left text for Arabic and Urdu

Built with React, Tailwind and Radix UI, and battle-tested on a live server.

Build yours in the browser Build with AI

See the live preview Download the latest release

docs.title: Two ways to build it
docs.text:
Config Builder: edit every option in a visual editor and watch the real loading screen update as you go. Paste links or upload your own images, videos and music; they are bundled into the download for you.

Build with AI: describe your server in plain words ("dark purple, our Discord and Tebex links, five rules") and the assistant builds the screen for you. Keep chatting to change anything.

Both export the same thing: a 4zam_loading resource with your config.json and files already inside.

docs.title: Install in 3 steps
docs.text:
1. Get the resource. Export it from the Config Builder, or download the stock version from the latest release.
  2. Unzip it into your resources so the folder is resources/4zam_loading.

  3. Add it to server.cfg and restart the server:

    ensure 4zam_loading

Full steps, updating and common fixes: Install & update and Troubleshooting.

docs.title: Editing by hand?
docs.text: Every config.json option is listed in the Config reference, generated from the source code so it always matches the release. You can also import an existing config.json into the Config Builder to keep editing it visually.

docs.title: 🎥 Background
docs.text:
Your loading screen background can be a static image or a video. If both are provided, the video takes priority.

📁 Remember: Place any images or videos inside the html/assets/ folder so they load correctly.

Quicker in the Config Builder

The Config Builder sets all of this under Background with a live preview, and Build with AI can set it up from a plain description. Every field with its type and default is in the Config reference: backgroundImage and backgroundVideo and videoAsAudio.

docs.title: 📷 Static Image Background
docs.text:
"backgroundImage": "./assets/path/to/background.png",
"backgroundVideo": ""

Static Image Notes

If you want to use a static image, leave "backgroundVideo" empty. Even static images receive subtle ambient movement and lighting effects for depth.

docs.title: 🎬 Video Background (Local WebM)
docs.text:
"backgroundVideo": "./assets/path/to/bg.webm"

Best Performance

Local video files load the fastest and avoid any YouTube embedding restrictions.

Supported formats:

  • .webm (recommended)
  • .mp4

Place your files inside:

html/assets/

docs.title: 📺 Video Background (YouTube)
docs.text:
"backgroundVideo": "https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=abc123"

Video Takes Priority

If "backgroundVideo" is set, the static "backgroundImage" will not be used.

docs.title: ⚠️ YouTube Embed Requirements & Error Handling
docs.text:
Error 153 is fixed in v1.3.0

FiveM loads loading screens from nui://, which sends no Referer, so YouTube used to reject every embed with "Error 153: video player configuration error". Since v1.3.0, YouTube links play in game through a small player page hosted at loadingscreen.4zam.dev, with sound, pause and volume working as usual. No setup is needed: paste a normal YouTube link.

YouTube videos still must meet a few requirements set by the video owner. If a video can't play, the loading screen automatically:

  • Moves on to your next video, or to your music, within about 15 seconds, and
  • Shows a notice only if every video fails, falling back to your static background image with animation.

docs.title: Required YouTube Settings
docs.text:
Make sure your video has:

  • Embedding enabled (YouTube Studio → Video → Settings → Permissions → “Allow embedding”)
  • No age restriction
  • No region/copyright blocks
  • Public or unlisted visibility

If any of these are missing, YouTube will block the embed request and the screen falls back as described above.

docs.title: How to Fix YouTube Videos That Won't Play
docs.text:
1. Open YouTube Studio
  2. Click Content
  3. Select the video used in your config
  4. Check the Restrictions column
  5. Fix any of the following issues:
    • Age-restricted → remove restriction
    • Region blocked → allow all locations
    • Embedding disabled → enable permissions

The YouTube player page needs loadingscreen.4zam.dev to be reachable. If it isn't, YouTube backgrounds fall back to your next video or music within about 8 seconds. Local video files never depend on it.

docs.title: Final Fallback: Use a Local WebM (Recommended)
docs.text:
If your video still refuses to embed, even after correcting settings:

Download the video and use a local .webm file instead. This completely bypasses YouTube’s restrictions.

Place the file here:

html/assets/webm/background.webm

Then update your config:

"backgroundVideo": "./assets/webm/background.webm"

This is the most reliable solution and prevents future YouTube policy issues.

docs.title: Automatic Fallback Behavior
docs.text:
If a YouTube or local video fails:

  • The screen moves on to the next video, or to your music
  • If every video fails, a notice explains the issue with a link to troubleshooting docs
  • The background animates using your static "backgroundImage"

This ensures the loading screen remains usable even during media failures.

Preview

docs.title: Video as the Audio Source
docs.text:
A background video can either be the audio (the player controls it: play/pause, scrub, volume) or play as a silent, looping background while the music player provides the audio. The videoAsAudio flag controls this:

"backgroundVideo": "./assets/webm/ambient.webm",
"videoAsAudio": false

Field details: videoAsAudio in the Config reference.

Smart default

If you don't set videoAsAudio, the behavior depends on your config:

  • With a music playlist → the video is muted and the music plays. (Music wins.)
  • Without any music → the video becomes the audio source, so the screen is never silent.

Set videoAsAudio explicitly to force either behavior regardless of the music playlist.

Pause the background video

In muted-ambient mode (videoAsAudio: false), a Pause Video button appears in the bottom-left controls so players can freeze or resume the looping background video.

docs.title: Multiple Background Videos (Playlist)
docs.text:
backgroundVideo accepts either a single URL string (the original shape) or an array of videos. With an array, the player gains forward/back controls to move between videos, and a playlist counter (e.g. 2 / 5) appears.

"backgroundVideo": [
  { "url": "./assets/webm/intro.webm",  "title": "Night Cruise", "subtitle": "The Vibe RP" },
  { "url": "https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=abc123", "title": "City Lights" },
  { "url": "./assets/webm/skyline.webm" }
]

Each entry takes url, plus an optional title and subtitle: see backgroundVideo in the Config reference.

Backwards compatible

A single string ("backgroundVideo": "./assets/webm/bg.webm") still works exactly as before. The array form is only needed when you want more than one video.

Default labels when title / subtitle are omitted

For any entry without metadata, the player falls back to your watermark:

  • title → your watermark name (watermark.label.text)
  • subtitle → your watermark subheading (watermark.subHeading)
  • cover art → your watermark logo (watermark.logo)

Entries can also be plain URL strings (["a.webm", "b.webm"]): those use these fallbacks for every field.

When a video fails

If a video in the list fails to load, it is skipped to the next one. If every video fails, the screen falls back to the music player (or the animated image background).

Muted-background playlists auto-cycle

In muted-ambient mode (videoAsAudio: false, with a music playlist), a multi-video list plays through automatically: each video plays in turn, then loops back to the first. There are no on-screen forward/back controls in this mode (those appear only when the video is the audio source), and a single video simply loops in place.

docs.title: Summary of Background Priority
docs.text: Priority Type Notes 1 YouTube Video Must allow embedding; otherwise fallback 2️ Local WEBM Fastest + most reliable 3️ Static Image Used when no video or video fails

docs.title: v1.3.1
docs.text:
• YouTube links are read the same way everywhere. The loading screen, the Config Builder preview and the AI assistant now share one YouTube link reader, so a link that previews correctly also plays in game.
    • A video link that also carries playlist details (&list=...&index=...) now plays just that video instead of the whole playlist, and keeps its start time (t= or start=).
    • Pure playlist and channel links are still not supported as backgrounds.
  • The license now points to the community hub at thevibe.4zam.dev.

docs.title: v1.3.0
docs.text:
• YouTube backgrounds work in FiveM again (Error 153 fixed). FiveM serves loading screens from nui://, which sends no Referer, so YouTube rejected every embed with "Error 153: video player configuration error". YouTube links now play in game through a small player page hosted at loadingscreen.4zam.dev, with sound, pause and volume working as before. See Background.
    • If a YouTube video still cannot play (embedding disabled, age restriction or the player page unreachable), the screen falls back to the next video or your music within about 15 seconds. If every video fails, a notice explains why.
    • Local MP4/WEBM backgrounds are unchanged and never use the hosted page.

docs.title: v1.2.2
docs.text: • Asset host migration and logo fix. The loading-screen assets (background video, music, images, watermark logo) now load from the dl.4zam.dev asset host at stable, URL-safe paths, since the previous host was retired. This also fixes a broken watermark logo caused by a filename with a space in it. No gameplay or config changes are required; if you maintain your own config.json, point its asset URLs at dl.4zam.dev. Code is unchanged from v1.2.0.

docs.title: v1.2.0
docs.text:
• Renamed the resource to 4zam_loading (previously gucci_loading). Updating an existing install: rename the resource folder to 4zam_loading and change your server.cfg line to ensure 4zam_loading. Fresh downloads already use the new name. See Setup.
  • Background videos are more reliable in FiveM. A video that silently freezes, or an embed that never starts, now falls back automatically instead of leaving a black screen. Background videos also always autoplay now, whether or not the video is the audio source.
  • Cleaner fullscreen on every monitor. The background video and images fill the screen edge to edge in a clean 16:9 with no black bars, on standard, ultrawide and 4:3 displays alike.

docs.title: v1.1.0
docs.text: • The on-screen keyboard key labels now automatically pick black or white for the highest contrast against your accent color, the same way the rest of the loading screen already did. Dark accent colors no longer render unreadable dark-on-dark key labels, and bright accents get crisp dark labels. The choice is WCAG AA legible for any color you pick. See Keyboard Overlay.

docs.title: v1.0.10
docs.text:
• Background videos now cycle automatically when used as a muted background, not only when the video is the audio source. With videoAsAudio off (a music playlist drives the audio), multiple backgroundVideo entries now play through in sequence and loop, instead of only the first one playing. See Background.
    • Automatic skip on error: if a video fails to load, the screen moves on to the next working video in the list, and only falls back to the animated background if every video fails.
    • The last remaining video loops smoothly instead of freezing on its final frame.

docs.title: v1.0.9
docs.text:
• Added full localization across the loading screen, the Config Builder, and the AI assistant, in 7 languages: English (US), English (UK), Spanish, German, French, Arabic, and Urdu. See Language & RTL.
    • Set the loading-screen language with a new top-level language field in config.json (for example "language": "ar"). Missing or unknown values stay English, so older configs are unaffected.
    • Right-to-left (RTL) text for Arabic and Urdu: each piece of text renders in its natural direction, with an Arabic/Urdu font bundled into the resource so it displays correctly offline. The screen keeps its normal layout (panels and watermark are not moved); physical controls such as the keyboard grid stay left-to-right by design.
    • The Config Builder auto-detects your browser language, adds a Language switcher in the settings menu, remembers your choice, and writes the language into your exported config.json automatically.
    • The AI assistant replies in your language.
    • Keyboard key-cap labels now follow language automatically (the existing keyboardShortcuts.locale still overrides).
  • Added localized per-field help hints in the Config Builder: click the ℹ️ info icon next to any field to reveal a short "how to fill this" explanation inline, in your language.
  • Added an AI-translation disclaimer in the Language menu, noting that non-English translations are AI generated.
  • Added a Terms and Conditions page (linked from the settings menu on the builder and AI pages).

docs.title: v1.0.8
docs.text:
• Added a free in-browser Config Builder on the website: edit every config.json option in a visual editor with color pickers, see a true-to-life live preview of the loading screen as you go, and export a ready-to-run gucci_loading.zip you drop straight into your server. No more editing config blind.
    • Paste a URL or upload a file for any image/video/audio; uploads are bundled into the download automatically.
    • Import an existing config.json, or upload a whole gucci_loading folder, to keep editing it. If it references local assets (./assets/...), add those files in the import dialog and they show up in the live preview right away.
    • Light / dark / system theme and your work auto-saves in the browser so a refresh never loses it.
  • Added a Build with AI assistant: describe your server in plain language and the assistant builds and edits your loading screen for you, live, no account needed. Includes a built-in support assistant that answers setup and troubleshooting questions right in the chat.
  • Gave the builder and AI pages a premium restyle: a frosted-glass UI with a single reactive accent that follows your chosen color across the whole interface, plus higher-contrast, more readable loading-screen text over busy backgrounds.
  • Added configurable title animation with curated presets and a sweeping sheen overlay, via watermark.label.animation and watermark.label.sheen. See Title Animation.
  • Added video as the audio source: a background video can be driven by the built-in player (play/pause, scrub, volume).
  • Added multiple background videos (playlist): backgroundVideo now accepts an array with per-video title/subtitle, forward/back controls, and a position counter. See Background.
  • Added the videoAsAudio toggle with a music-aware default: with a music playlist the video is muted and the music plays; with no music the video becomes the audio source.
  • Added a Pause Video control shown only in muted-ambient mode.
  • Added gallery lightbox navigation: open an image and browse the gallery with on-screen arrows or the arrow keys, with position dots. See Gallery Panel.
  • Reorganized the documentation: split Background into its own page.

docs.title: v1.0.7
docs.text:
• Added compact keyboard localization support through keyboardShortcuts.layout and keyboardShortcuts.locale.
  • Added support for multiple compact keyboard layout styles:
    • ansi
    • iso
    • jis
  • Improved keyboard overlay rendering so layout-specific key labels can be displayed without changing the compact design.
  • Added compatibility handling for symbol-based key aliases such as ~ on the top-left key.
  • Added a dedicated Custom Panel Configuration documentation page.
  • Added support for preset custom panel icons through a built-in icon registry.
  • Fixed an issue where multiple custom social headers could be highlighted/selected at the same time if they shared the same type.
  • Updated social header selection logic to use an internal runtime ID so duplicate custom entries now behave correctly.

docs.title: v1.0.6
docs.text:
• Added fixed height and scroll functionality to the team members panel.
  • Added a configuration item to add custom panels to the right-hand side of the loading screen.
  • Fixed parallax animation to prevent zooming in on images, which was causing weird behaviors.
  • Improved parallax animation and effect.
  • Cleaned up and maintained the codebase.
  • Updated all asset paths to use fivemanage URLs for a smaller delivery package.

docs.title: v1.0.5
docs.text:
• Updated documentation to recommend using WebM as the preferred video format for loading screens due to better compatibility with FiveM's NUI.
  • Updated fxmanifest.lua to include paths for importing WebM files. Ensure the correct file paths are included for WebM assets when upgrading.
  • Check the Upgrade Guide for detailed instructions on updating fxmanifest.lua and other changes.

docs.title: v1.0.4
docs.text:
• Added graceful YouTube/local video failure handling with a troubleshooting modal and docs link.
    • Implementation Explanation
    • Troubleshooting Guide
  • Improved detection of YouTube embed restrictions (e.g., error 153).
  • Added support for custom social media icons through config
    • Setup Guide

docs.title: v1.0.3
docs.text:
• Introduced a fixed-height container with scroll support to ensure usability when the gallery contains a large number of images.
  • Added the ability to fully disable the music player via configuration.
  • Implemented a defaultVolume parameter to allow setting the initial playback volume of the music player on the loading screen.

docs.title: v1.0.2
docs.text:
• Fixed an issue where the UI would lose hover effects if there were too many gallery images
  • Added check on gallery item count in order to disable gallery

docs.title: v1.0.1
docs.text:
• Fixed an issue where the UI would break if no social media options were enabled in the config.
  • Made the info button label on social cards configurable via config.json.
  • Social media buttons now open their configured links when clicked.

docs.title: v1.0.0
docs.text:
• Initial release
  • Full keyboard overlay support
  • YouTube and MP4 background support
  • Configurable music player

docs.title: Config reference
docs.text:
Every option in config.json, generated from the loading screen's source code for the current release.

You rarely need this page: the Config Builder and Build with AI write config.json for you and show a live preview. Use it when you edit the file by hand.

config.json lives at html/config.json inside the 4zam_loading resource. Restart the resource after editing it. Images, videos and audio can be full URLs or paths inside the resource such as ./assets/bg.webm. Values are shown the way you write them in JSON.

docs.title: Fields at a glance
docs.text: Field Type Builder What it does language string Settings menu Language of the loading-screen text. mirrorLayout boolean config.json only Mirror the whole layout right to left (panels and watermark swap sides). selectedColor string Brand & Color Accent color used across the screen (title highlight, buttons, cards). backgroundImage string Background Background image: a URL or a path inside the resource such as ./assets/bg.png. backgroundVideo string or (string or object)[] or null Background Background video. videoUrl string config.json only Legacy single-video field from early versions, read only when backgroundVideo is absent. videoAsAudio boolean Background Whether the background video is the audio source. watermark object Brand & Color The server name, subheading and logo shown in the corner of the screen. socialHeaders object[] Social Links Social and link cards in the header (Discord, store and so on). rules string[] Rules Server rules shown in the Rules panel, one string per rule. teamMembers object[] Team Staff cards shown in the Team panel. customPanels object[] Custom Panels Extra tabs with your own list content (updates, guides, jobs and so on). gallery object[] Gallery Images in the Gallery panel. keyboardShortcuts object Keyboard Keybind hints shown on the on-screen keyboard. music object[] Music Music playlist (.mp3). defaultVolume number Music Starting player volume in percent.

docs.title: language
docs.text:
Language of the loading-screen text. Arabic (ar) and Urdu (ur) render right to left. Missing or unknown values fall back to English.

Type: string, optional.

Allowed values: 12 allowed values.

Default: "en".

Set for you: the builder writes the language you pick in its settings menu.

docs.title: language allowed values
docs.text: Value What it does "en" English "en-GB" English (UK) "es" Español "de" Deutsch "fr" Français "it" Italiano "nl" Nederlands "pl" Polski "pt" Português "hi" हिन्दी "ar" العربية, right to left "ur" اردو, right to left

docs.title: mirrorLayout
docs.text:
Mirror the whole layout right to left (panels and watermark swap sides). Independent of language, which only changes text direction.

Type: boolean, optional.

Default: false.

Not in the builder: set it in config.json by hand.

docs.title: selectedColor
docs.text:
Accent color used across the screen (title highlight, buttons, cards). Hex (#7C3AED) or rgb()/rgba()/hsl()/hsla(). Anything else falls back to the default.

Type: string.

Default: "#FF8A4D".

Edit it in the Config Builder under Brand & Color.

docs.title: backgroundImage
docs.text:
Background image: a URL or a path inside the resource such as ./assets/bg.png. Shown when there is no video, or when every video fails.

Type: string.

Default: "".

Edit it in the Config Builder under Background.

docs.title: backgroundVideo
docs.text:
Background video. Either one URL (a local .webm/.mp4 path or a YouTube link) or a list of videos the player can skip between. A video takes priority over backgroundImage.

Type: string or (string or object)[] or null, optional.

Edit it in the Config Builder under Background.

Key Type Allowed values Default Description backgroundVideo[].url string Video URL: a local .webm/.mp4 path or a YouTube link. backgroundVideo[].title string, optional Name shown in the player for this video. Falls back to the watermark title. backgroundVideo[].subtitle string, optional Line shown under the title. Falls back to the watermark subheading.

docs.title: videoUrl
docs.text:
Legacy single-video field from early versions, read only when backgroundVideo is absent. Use backgroundVideo instead.

Type: string, optional.

Not in the builder: set it in config.json by hand.

docs.title: videoAsAudio
docs.text:
Whether the background video is the audio source. true: the player controls the video (play, pause, scrub, volume). false: the video loops muted and the player drives the music playlist. When omitted, the video is the audio source only if there is no music playlist.

Type: boolean, optional.

Edit it in the Config Builder under Background.

docs.title: watermark
docs.text:
The server name, subheading and logo shown in the corner of the screen.

Type: object.

Edit it in the Config Builder under Brand & Color.

Key Type Allowed values Default Description watermark.label object The title line. watermark.label.text string The main title text, usually your server name. watermark.label.colorWordCount number 1 How many words of text, counted from the start, get the accent color. watermark.label.animation string, optional 9 allowed values "wave" Title animation preset. Missing or unknown values use wave. The sheen (below) layers on top of any preset. watermark.label.sheen boolean, optional true Sweeping light sheen across the title. Set false to turn it off. watermark.subHeading string Smaller line shown under the title. watermark.logo string Logo image: a URL or a path inside the resource.

docs.title: watermark.label.animation allowed values
docs.text: Value What it does "none" No motion: the title fades in and stays still. "wave" Each letter gently bobs up and down in sequence. The default. "wave-reverse" The same bob, staggered right to left. "bounce" A snappier, springier hop on each letter. "ripple" Letters scale-pop in sequence, like a travelling ripple. "sway" The whole title rocks gently left and right. "reveal" The title wipes in left to right, holds, then wipes out, on a loop. "slam" The title punches in with a sharp impact, repeating now and then. "pulse" The title thumps to a beat, with a synced underline glow.

docs.title: socialHeaders
docs.text:
Social and link cards in the header (Discord, store and so on). Cards with enabled: false are hidden.

Type: object[].

Edit it in the Config Builder under Social Links.

Key Type Allowed values Default Description socialHeaders[].type string "discord", "instagram", "telegram", "youtube", "tiktok", "custom" Platform icon to show, lowercase and spelled exactly. Use custom to supply your own icon image. socialHeaders[].imagePath string, optional Custom icon image (URL or resource path). Used with type: "custom". socialHeaders[].imageWidth string, optional Custom icon width, any CSS size such as 3vw or 32px. socialHeaders[].imageHeight string, optional Custom icon height, any CSS size such as 3vh or 32px. socialHeaders[].cardLabel string Card title. socialHeaders[].cardInfo string Short description under the card title. socialHeaders[].link string URL opened by the card button. socialHeaders[].buttonLabel string Button text. When empty, a localized default such as "Join" is used. socialHeaders[].enabled boolean true Show this card on the screen.

docs.title: rules
docs.text:
Server rules shown in the Rules panel, one string per rule. Use \n for a line break. Five or six short rules read best.

Type: string[], optional.

Edit it in the Config Builder under Rules.

docs.title: teamMembers
docs.text:
Staff cards shown in the Team panel.

Type: object[], optional.

Edit it in the Config Builder under Team.

Key Type Allowed values Default Description teamMembers[].name string Display name. teamMembers[].role string Role or position shown under the name. teamMembers[].discord string Discord username, or any short label. teamMembers[].image string Avatar image (URL or resource path); square images look best.

docs.title: customPanels
docs.text:
Extra tabs with your own list content (updates, guides, jobs and so on).

Type: object[], optional.

Edit it in the Config Builder under Custom Panels.

Key Type Allowed values Default Description customPanels[].panelPosition number Where the tab sits in the tab row; lower numbers come first. Defaults to the panel's position in the list. customPanels[].uniqueId string Unique id for the panel, such as updates. Must differ between panels. Defaults to panel-<n>. customPanels[].buttonLabel string Tab button text. customPanels[].icon string 41 preset names Tab icon: a preset icon name (an fa- prefix and capitals are ignored) or an image. An image is any value ending in .png, .jpg, .jpeg, .gif, .webp or .svg, or starting with http://, https://, ./, ../ or /. Anything else shows the default megaphone icon. Inline SVG code is not supported. customPanels[].cardHeaderLabel string Heading at the top of the panel. customPanels[].singularLabel string Label for one entry, such as Update or Tip. customPanels[].entries string[] The list items, one string each.

docs.title: customPanels[].icon preset names

Preset names: "circle", "bullhorn", "users", "image", "star", "shield", "shield-halved", "gavel", "briefcase", "wrench", "screwdriver-wrench", "tools", "car", "house", "home", "store", "shop", "gift", "crown", "music", "newspaper", "globe", "handshake", "trophy", "flag", "bolt", "heart", "bell", "map", "book", "scroll", "list", "gear", "cog", "hammer", "info", "circle-info", "clipboard", "comments", "phone", "wallet".

docs.title: gallery
docs.text:
Images in the Gallery panel. Players can open one and browse with the arrow keys.

Type: object[], optional.

Edit it in the Config Builder under Gallery.

Key Type Allowed values Default Description gallery[].path string Image URL or resource path; landscape images look best.

docs.title: keyboardShortcuts
docs.text:
Keybind hints shown on the on-screen keyboard.

Type: object.

Edit it in the Config Builder under Keyboard.

Key Type Allowed values Default Description keyboardShortcuts.layout string, optional "ansi", "iso", "jis" "ansi" Physical keyboard layout to draw. keyboardShortcuts.locale string, optional Locale for the key labels, such as de-DE. It translates special keys (Shift, Enter) and sets the letter layout: German shows QWERTZ, French AZERTY and everything else QWERTY. When omitted, follows language. keyboardShortcuts.keys object[] The highlighted keys. keyboardShortcuts.keys[].key string 72 allowed values The key to highlight. Case does not matter (Left Arrow matches LEFT ARROW); letters and numbers are written as themselves. A key your layout does not draw is never highlighted. keyboardShortcuts.keys[].onFoot string or null Hint shown while on foot, or null for none. keyboardShortcuts.keys[].inCar string or null Hint shown while in a vehicle, or null for none.

docs.title: keyboardShortcuts.keys[].key allowed values

docs.title: 🧩 Custom Panel Configuration
docs.text:
Custom panels let you add your own fully customizable tabs to the loading screen. Use them for updates, server info, guides, economy details, jobs, starter tips, store links, whitelist info or any other structured content you want players to see while loading in.

Quicker in the Config Builder

The Config Builder sets all of this under Custom Panels with a live preview, and Build with AI can set it up from a plain description. Every field with its type and default is in the Config reference: customPanels.

docs.title: JSON Structure
docs.text:
"customPanels": [
    {
        "panelPosition": 1,
        "uniqueId": "updates",
        "buttonLabel": "Updates",
        "icon": "bullhorn",
        "cardHeaderLabel": "Latest City Updates",
        "singularLabel": "Update",
        "entries": [
            "Daily job based quests with reward system",
            "Loot boxes with provable fairness and security",
            "New 200+ lore friendly vehicles added with more on the way"
        ]
    }
]

docs.title: Field Breakdown
docs.text:
Each panel takes panelPosition, uniqueId, buttonLabel, icon, cardHeaderLabel, singularLabel and entries (one string per list item). What each does, with types, is in the Config reference.

Multiple Custom Panels Supported

You can add as many custom panels as you want by adding more objects to the customPanels array.

Unique IDs Must Be Unique

Every custom panel must use a different uniqueId. Reusing the same ID can cause the wrong panel to be opened or rendered.

docs.title: Example: Multiple Custom Panels
docs.text:
"customPanels": [
    {
        "panelPosition": 1,
        "uniqueId": "updates",
        "buttonLabel": "Updates",
        "icon": "bullhorn",
        "cardHeaderLabel": "Latest City Updates",
        "singularLabel": "Update",
        "entries": [
            "Daily job based quests with reward system",
            "New 200+ lore friendly vehicles added with more on the way",
            "Vehicle rarity system with Discord webhook integrations"
        ]
    },
    {
        "panelPosition": 3,
        "uniqueId": "starter-guide",
        "buttonLabel": "Starter Guide",
        "icon": "book",
        "cardHeaderLabel": "Getting Started",
        "singularLabel": "Tip",
        "entries": [
            "Visit City Hall first to pick up your starter items",
            "Use the radial menu to access quick actions",
            "Join the Discord for announcements and support"
        ]
    }
]

docs.title: Panel Order (panelPosition)
docs.text: panelPosition controls where the button appears in the header row.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
"customPanels": [
    {
        "panelPosition": 1,
        "uniqueId": "updates",
        "buttonLabel": "Updates",
        "icon": "bullhorn",
        "cardHeaderLabel": "Latest City Updates",
        "singularLabel": "Update",
        "entries": ["Example update"]
    },
    {
        "panelPosition": 2,
        "uniqueId": "guide",
        "buttonLabel": "Guide",
        "icon": "book",
        "cardHeaderLabel": "Starter Guide",
        "singularLabel": "Tip",
        "entries": ["Example tip"]
    }
]

In this example:

  • Updates appears before Guide
  • lower panelPosition values are placed earlier
  • each position should ideally be unique for best results

Recommended Usage

Use simple values like 1, 2, 3, 4, etc. to keep tab ordering predictable and easy to manage.

docs.title: Choosing a uniqueId
docs.text: The uniqueId is used internally by the loading screen to track which custom panel is being opened.

docs.title: Recommended format
docs.text:
• lowercase
  • no spaces
  • use hyphens if needed

docs.title: Good examples
docs.text:
• updates
  • starter-guide
  • city-rules
  • economy-info

docs.title: Avoid
docs.text:
• duplicate IDs
  • IDs with spaces
  • changing IDs frequently after release unless necessary

Best Practice

Treat uniqueId like an internal key, not a visible label. Players will see buttonLabel, not uniqueId.

docs.title: Supported Icon Types
docs.text: The icon field supports several formats.

docs.title: 1. Preset icon names (recommended)
docs.text: These are the easiest to use and are the best option for most servers.

docs.title: Example
docs.text: "icon": "bullhorn"

docs.title: Supported preset icon names
docs.text:
The full list is generated from the icons the loading screen ships: see icon preset names. Names ignore capitals and an fa- prefix.

Preset Icons Are Preferred

Preset icon names are the easiest option to document, maintain and style consistently.

docs.title: 2. fa- prefixed preset names
docs.text: You may also use the same preset names with the fa- prefix.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
"icon": "fa-bullhorn"

This works the same as:

"icon": "bullhorn"

docs.title: 3. Custom image path or URL
docs.text: You can use a local asset path or external image URL instead of a preset icon name.

docs.title: Example: Local asset
docs.text: "icon": "./assets/icons/store.png"

docs.title: Example: External URL
docs.text:
"icon": "https://your-cdn.com/icons/store-icon.png"

Supported image formats include:

  • .png
  • .jpg
  • .jpeg
  • .gif
  • .webp
  • .svg

Use Small, Clean Icons

Custom icon images should be square or close to square for best visual results inside the header button.

docs.title: 4. Inline SVG string (no longer supported)
docs.text: Inline SVG code in icon is no longer rendered: it was removed because config-supplied SVG markup is a security risk. Save the icon as an .svg file and use its path or URL instead (option 3).

docs.title: Example
docs.text: "icon": "<svg viewBox='0 0 24 24' fill='currentColor'><path d='...'/></svg>"

docs.title: Fallback Behavior
docs.text:
If the icon value is invalid or unsupported, the loading screen falls back to the default icon (a megaphone).

Fallback Icon

Invalid panel icons automatically fall back to the default icon instead of breaking the UI.

docs.title: Example: Preset Icon
docs.text:
"customPanels": [
    {
        "panelPosition": 2,
        "uniqueId": "economy",
        "buttonLabel": "Economy",
        "icon": "wallet",
        "cardHeaderLabel": "City Economy Info",
        "singularLabel": "Detail",
        "entries": [
            "Starter cash is provided when you first join",
            "Jobs and side hustles are the best way to build income",
            "Illegal routes carry higher risk and reward"
        ]
    }
]

docs.title: Example: Custom Image Icon
docs.text:
"customPanels": [
    {
        "panelPosition": 2,
        "uniqueId": "store",
        "buttonLabel": "Store",
        "icon": "./assets/icons/store.png",
        "cardHeaderLabel": "Support the Server",
        "singularLabel": "Perk",
        "entries": [
            "Vehicle packs available in the store",
            "Exclusive cosmetic rewards available",
            "Check the store for supporter packages"
        ]
    }
]

docs.title: Tips for Best Results
docs.text:
• Keep buttonLabel short so it fits nicely in the animated header buttons.
  • Keep cardHeaderLabel descriptive and readable.
  • Use a clear singularLabel that matches the purpose of the panel.
  • Keep entries short enough to scan quickly during loading.
  • Use preset icons whenever possible for the cleanest look.
  • Use unique panelPosition values for predictable ordering.
  • Use unique, stable uniqueId values.

docs.title: Recommended Icon Formats for Custom Image Icons
docs.text:
For best results:

  • SVG (preferred)

    • Sharp at any size
    • Great for logos and simple icons
    • Small file size

  • PNG (transparent background preferred)

    • Best for custom branded icons
    • Clean presentation inside the header buttons

  • JPEG / JPG (supported but not ideal)

    • Works, but transparency is not supported
    • Usually less suitable for compact icon buttons

Avoid:

  • low-resolution images
  • very wide logos
  • very tall aspect ratios
  • images with large solid backgrounds
  • photos instead of icon-style graphics

docs.title: Full Example
docs.text:

    {
        "panelPosition": 1,
        "uniqueId": "updates",
        "buttonLabel": "Updates",
        "icon": "bullhorn",
        "cardHeaderLabel": "Latest City Updates",
        "singularLabel": "Update",
        "entries": [
            "Daily job based quests with reward system",
            "Loot boxes with provable fairness and security",
            "New 200+ lore friendly vehicles added with more on the way",
            "Vehicle rarity system with Discord webhook integrations"
        ]
    },
    {
        "panelPosition": 2,
        "uniqueId": "guide",
        "buttonLabel": "Guide",
        "icon": "book",
        "cardHeaderLabel": "Starter Guide",
        "singularLabel": "Tip",
        "entries": [
            "Visit City Hall first to collect your starter items",
            "Use the radial menu for quick access to important features",
            "Join the Discord to stay up to date on events and support"
        ]
    },
    {
        "panelPosition": 3,
        "uniqueId": "store",
        "buttonLabel": "Store",
        "icon": "./assets/icons/store.png",
        "cardHeaderLabel": "Support the Server",
        "singularLabel": "Perk",
        "entries": [
            "Store packages help support development",
            "Exclusive cosmetic rewards are available",
            "Visit the store for the latest supporter options"
        ]
    }
]

docs.title: 🖼️ Gallery Panel Configuration
docs.text:
The Gallery Panel appears on the loading screen and allows you to showcase images such as cars, team highlights, banners or community events.

You can customize the images shown by editing the gallery array in your configuration file.

Quicker in the Config Builder

The Config Builder sets all of this under Gallery with a live preview, and Build with AI can set it up from a plain description. Every field with its type and default is in the Config reference: gallery.

docs.title: JSON Structure
docs.text:
"gallery": [
    { "path": "./assets/png/headshot.png" },
    { "path": "./assets/png/bluebmw.png" },
    { "path": "./assets/png/fmbanner.png" },
    { "path": "./assets/png/2gtrs.png" },
    { "path": "./assets/png/vibe.png" },
    { "path": "./assets/png/supra2.png" }
]

docs.title: Field Breakdown
docs.text:
Each image takes one field, path: a URL or a path inside the resource such as ./assets/png/headshot.png (files go in html/assets/). See gallery.

Recommended Image Format

Use .png or .jpg images in landscape orientation for best visual balance.

Aspect Ratio Tip

For a clean layout, try to keep all gallery images at a consistent resolution (e.g. 1280x720 or 1920x1080).

docs.title: Viewing Images (Lightbox)
docs.text:
Clicking any thumbnail opens the image in a full-size lightbox. From there you can move through the gallery:

  • On-screen arrows: left/right arrows on the sides of the image jump to the previous/next picture.
  • Keyboard: the ← and → arrow keys navigate, and Esc closes the lightbox.

Navigation wraps around: going back from the first image shows the last, and forward from the last returns to the first.

Single image

The navigation arrows only appear when the gallery has more than one image. No extra configuration is needed: navigation works over your existing gallery array.

Lightbox Preview

Gallery Panel Preview

Automatic Gallery Tab Hiding

The gallery tab is automatically hidden if the gallery array is empty ([ ]) or omitted entirely from the config. To disable the gallery feature, simply remove the gallery entry or ensure the array contains no images.

docs.text:
The keyboard overlay appears on the loading screen and visually highlights keybinds to help new players learn essential controls. You can customize the compact keyboard layout, displayed language and individual shortcuts using the keyboardShortcuts configuration.

Quicker in the Config Builder

The Config Builder sets all of this under Keyboard with a live preview, and Build with AI can set it up from a plain description. Every field with its type and default is in the Config reference: keyboardShortcuts.

    "layout": "ansi",
    "locale": "en-US",
    "keys": [

            "key": "~",

            "inCar": "Put on seatbelt"
        },
        {
            "key": "Left Arrow",
            "onFoot": null,
            "inCar": "Left Indicator"

            "inCar": "Right Indicator"

docs.title: Field Breakdown
docs.text:
• layout (optional): which compact keyboard is drawn, ansi, iso or jis.
  • locale (optional): how special key labels are shown, for example en-US, de-DE, fr-FR, es-ES, pt-BR, ar, zh-CN or ja-JP. When omitted it follows language.
  • keys: the keybinds to highlight. Each has a key, plus onFoot and inCar tooltip text (null for none).

Types and defaults are in the Config reference.

Multiple Contexts

You can define different behaviors for the same key depending on whether the player is on foot or in a vehicle.

Optional Settings

If layout or locale are omitted, the loading screen will fall back to default values. Existing configs without these fields will continue to work.

docs.title: Keyboard Layouts
docs.text:
The loading screen uses a compact keyboard overlay and supports multiple layout styles:

Layout Description ansi Standard US-style compact keyboard layout iso Common European-style compact keyboard layout jis Japanese-style compact keyboard layout

What layout changes

The selected layout affects how symbol keys are displayed in the overlay. It does not change your server's actual game keybinds: it only changes the visual keyboard preview.

docs.title: Locale / Language Display
docs.text:
The locale field changes the displayed labels for special keys such as:

  • Tab
  • Caps Lock
  • Enter
  • Shift
  • Ctrl
  • Alt
  • Space

Example:

"keyboardShortcuts": {
    "layout": "iso",
    "locale": "de-DE",
    "keys": [
        {
            "key": "LALT",
            "onFoot": "Third eye view",
            "inCar": null
        }
    ]
}

This would render the keyboard using the ISO layout and German-style special key labels.

docs.title: Accepted Key Names
docs.text: For best results, use the exact key label shown in the keyboard overlay preview. Case does not matter. The complete list of names every layout accepts is generated from the overlay itself: see keyboard key names.

docs.title: Standard Named Keys
docs.text: Actual Key JSON Key Name Left ALT LALT Right ALT RALT Left CTRL LCTRL Right CTRL RCTRL Left SHIFT LSHIFT Right SHIFT RSHIFT Space Bar SPACE Backspace BACKSPACE Enter ENTER Tab TAB Caps Lock CAPS LOCK Left Arrow Left Arrow Right Arrow Right Arrow Up Arrow Up Arrow Down Arrow Down Arrow Windows Key WIN

docs.title: Letters and Numbers
docs.text:
You can use normal letters and numbers directly:

{ "key": "A", "onFoot": "Action", "inCar": null }
{ "key": "1", "onFoot": null, "inCar": "Seat position" }

docs.title: Symbol Keys
docs.text:
Symbol keys should use the visible symbol shown in the compact keyboard overlay.

Examples:

Key JSON Key Name Tilde / top-left symbol key ~ Minus - Equals = Left Bracket [ Right Bracket ] Backslash \ Semicolon ; Quote ' Comma , Period . Slash /

Top-left key compatibility

The top-left symbol key accepts ~. Existing configs using ` are still supported for compatibility.

Naming Matters

Special named keys must match the supported values exactly. For example, use LALT instead of Alt, and SPACE instead of Spacebar.

docs.title: Tips for Best Results
docs.text:
• Keep tooltips short and action-focused.
  • Use the same layout that best matches your community's keyboard style.
  • Use the same locale as the language used throughout your loading screen.
  • For symbol keys, use the exact symbol shown in the overlay preview.
  • Avoid repeating the same key across multiple entries unless you intentionally want different onFoot and inCar behavior.
Keyboard Overlay Preview

docs.title: 🌐 Language & Right-to-Left (RTL)
docs.text:
The loading screen, the in-browser Config Builder and the Build with AI assistant are fully localized. Pick the language your community speaks and the whole experience follows, including right-to-left text for Arabic and Urdu.

Quicker in the Config Builder

The Config Builder sets all of this with a live preview, and Build with AI can set it up from a plain description. Every field with its type and default is in the Config reference: language.

docs.title: Supported languages
docs.text: The full list of language codes, with each language's name and text direction, is generated from the code in the Config reference.

docs.title: Setting the loading-screen language
docs.text:
Add a top-level language field to your config.json. Every player connecting to your server sees the loading screen in that language.

{
    "language": "ar",
    "selectedColor": "#7C3AED",
    "...": "rest of your config"
}
  • Set it to any code from the language list.
  • For ar or ur the text automatically renders right to left (see below).
  • If language is missing or not recognized, the screen stays English (LTR): so existing configs from older versions keep working unchanged.

Building in the Config Builder?

You usually do not need to edit this by hand. The builder sets language for you (see below).

docs.title: In the Config Builder and AI assistant
docs.text:
Open the Config Builder or Build with AI:

  • The interface auto-detects your browser language on first visit.
  • A Language option in the settings (gear) menu lets you switch at any time, and your choice is remembered.
  • The AI assistant replies in your language: describe your server in Arabic, Spanish, German, etc. and it answers in kind.
  • Every field has a localized help hint: click the small ℹ️ info icon next to a label to reveal a short "how to fill this" explanation inline, in your language. Click again to hide it.
  • When you export, the language you are building in is written into your config.json automatically, so the loading screen ships in the same language. You can always change the language field afterward.

About non-English translations

The interface translations are AI generated and reviewed, and may not be perfect. The Language menu notes this, and the Terms and Conditions are provided in English, which is the authoritative version.

docs.title: Right-to-left text (Arabic & Urdu)
docs.text:
Setting the language to ar or ur makes the text render correctly right-to-left in each component, while keeping the screen's normal layout:

  • Each piece of text (chrome and your own content) is shown in its natural direction. Arabic/Urdu reads right-to-left and right-aligns; Latin text stays left-to-right.
  • An Arabic/Urdu font is bundled with the resource, so text renders correctly even if the player's machine has no Arabic font installed.
  • Your own content (rules, team names, panel text) is shown as you wrote it, in the correct direction.

Language does not move the panels or watermark - it only fixes the text. The screen keeps its normal layout.

docs.title: Keyboard
docs.text:
The keyboard overlay adapts to your language automatically:

  • Key-cap labels (Shift, Enter, Ctrl, etc.) are translated. The keys never change size for longer translations, so the layout never breaks.
  • Physical layout follows the language: German shows QWERTZ, French shows AZERTY, and the rest use QWERTY. The letters sit where that language's real keyboard puts them.

If you ever want to pin a specific key-cap language regardless of language, the keyboardShortcuts.locale field still works as an override. In the Config Builder you no longer type key names by hand: click a keybind's key field and press the actual key on your keyboard, and it is filled in for you. See Keyboard Overlay.

docs.title: What is and isn't translated
docs.text:
• Translated: all of the product's own interface text: buttons, labels, status text, dialogs, the AI assistant's replies.
  • Not translated: the content you write: your server rules, team member names and roles, social card text, track titles, panel entries. Those stay exactly as you enter them (and display correctly in RTL).

docs.title: Adding a language
docs.text: The architecture is built so a new language is a single file. If you would like to contribute one (or request one), reach out on the community hub: a new locale is one translation file plus one line in the locale registry, with no other code changes.

docs.title: 🎵 Music Player Configuration
docs.text:
The Music Player plays a rotating playlist during the loading screen, complete with track titles, artist names and optional cover art.

Customize your music experience by modifying the music array in your configuration file.

Quicker in the Config Builder

The Config Builder sets all of this under Music with a live preview, and Build with AI can set it up from a plain description. Every field with its type and default is in the Config reference: music and defaultVolume.

docs.title: JSON Structure
docs.text:
"music": [
  {
    "path": "./assets/mp3/1008gs.mp3",
    "title": "1008 Grams",
    "artist": "OT7 Quanny",
    "image": null
  }
]

docs.title: Field Breakdown
docs.text:
Each track takes path (the .mp3 file), title, artist and an optional image for cover art (null when unused). Types are in the Config reference.

Audio Format Support

Only .mp3 files are supported at this time. Make sure all audio files are properly encoded and placed under assets/mp3/.

Track Rotation

Tracks rotate automatically in order. The player includes play, pause, skip and volume control functionality.

Playlist Counter

When more than one track is configured, a small position counter (e.g. 2 / 5) appears at the top-right of the player card.

docs.title: Doubles as the Video Controller
docs.text:
When a background video is the audio source (videoAsAudio: true, or left out with no music playlist), this same player controls the video instead of the mp3 playlist: play/pause, scrub and volume all drive the video, and the "now playing" text comes from each video's title / subtitle. With multiple videos, the forward/back buttons and the position counter work just like the music playlist.

See Background for how to configure single or multiple background videos and the videoAsAudio toggle.

When does the player show?

The player appears when there is an mp3 playlist or a video acting as the audio source. In muted-ambient mode (videoAsAudio: false) the player controls the mp3 playlist while the video loops silently behind it.

docs.title: Optional Album Art
docs.text:
If you'd like to show cover art or thumbnails per track, provide the image field:

"image": "./assets/path/to/cover_art.png"

Image files should ideally be square (1:1 aspect ratio) and under 500KB for fast load times.

docs.title: Optional Default Volume Setting
docs.text:
To set the initial volume level of the music player, add the following entry to your config:

"defaultVolume": 100

This value accepts a number from 0 to 100, representing the percentage volume on first load.

Music Player UI Preview

Automatic Music Player Hiding

The music player tab is automatically hidden if the music array is empty ([ ]) or omitted entirely from the config. To disable the music player, simply remove the music entry or ensure the array contains no entries.

docs.title: 🎨 Customization Guide
docs.text:
You customize the look and feel of the loading screen by editing the config.json file located in the html directory of the package. Each area has its own focused page: start here, then jump to the section you want.

📁 Remember: Place any images, videos or audio files inside the html/assets/ folder so they load correctly in the UI.

Quicker in the Config Builder

The Config Builder sets all of this with a live preview, and Build with AI can set it up from a plain description. Every field with its type and default is in the Config reference: selectedColor.

docs.title: Overall Theme Color
docs.text:
Customize the main highlight UI color used across the screen:

"selectedColor": "#ff007b"

Color Format

Accepts hex (#ff007b) and rgb(), rgba(), hsl() or hsla() values. Anything else falls back to the default color.

docs.title: What You Can Customize
docs.text: Area Page 🎥 Background (image / video / playlist) Background 🏷️ Watermark (server name + logo) Watermark ✨ Title animation Title Animation 🧷 Social headers & custom icons Social Headers 📜 Rules panel Rules Panel 👥 Team panel Team Panel 🖼️ Gallery grid Gallery Grid 🧩 Custom panel Custom Panel ⌨️ Keyboard overlay Keyboard Overlay 🎵 Music player Music Player

docs.title: YouTube embed requirements & error handling
docs.text:
YouTube backgrounds work in FiveM (since v1.3.0). If one will not play, the video owner's settings usually block it: it needs embedding allowed, no age restriction, no region blocks and public or unlisted visibility. When a video fails, the screen moves on to your next video or your music, and falls back to your background image if every video fails.

Full details are on the Background page, and step-by-step fixes in Troubleshooting.

docs.title: 📜 Rules Panel Configuration
docs.text:
The rules panel appears on the right-hand side of the loading screen and displays your server’s key guidelines.

You can fully customize these rules by modifying the rules array in your config file.

Quicker in the Config Builder

The Config Builder sets all of this under Rules with a live preview, and Build with AI can set it up from a plain description. Every field with its type and default is in the Config reference: rules.

docs.title: JSON Structure
docs.text:
"rules": [
    "No griefing or trolling other players.",
    "Respect all admins and staff decisions.",
    "No hacking, exploiting, or modding\nin unfair ways.",
    "Keep your behavior mature\nand respectful at all times.",
    "Do not spam the chat\nor use slurs or hate speech."
]

Each entry in the array represents one rule. You can use \n inside strings to create intentional line breaks.

Formatting Notes

  • Add each rule as a quoted string inside the array.
  • You can insert \n for line breaks in longer rules.

docs.title: Suggested Limit
docs.text:
How Many Rules?

It's recommended to display no more than 5–6 rules to keep the panel readable and visually clean.

You’re free to experiment with more, but longer lists may appear cluttered depending on your screen layout and font size.

Rules Panel Preview

docs.title: Install & update
docs.text:
The fastest path is the Config Builder or Build with AI: design your screen, export it and you get a ready-to-run 4zam_loading resource with your settings and files inside.

Build yours in the browser

docs.title: Download
docs.text:
Use the zip you exported from the builder, or the stock version:

  1. Open the latest release.
  2. Download 4zam_loading.zip.
  3. Extract it into your server's resources so the folder is resources/4zam_loading.

The folder name matters: it must match the ensure line below.

docs.title: Add to server.cfg
docs.text:
ensure 4zam_loading

Then restart your server. The loading screen shows the next time a player connects.

Only one loading screen

FiveM shows one loading screen. If another resource also declares a loadscreen (an older loading screen, or one bundled with a framework), stop or remove it so it does not take over.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
All settings live in one file:

resources/4zam_loading/html/config.json
  • Easiest: import that file into the Config Builder, change what you want and export again.
  • By hand: every option is in the Config reference. Put your own images, videos and music in html/assets/ and point to them as ./assets/your-file.webm, or use full URLs.

After editing, restart the resource (restart 4zam_loading) or the server.

docs.title: Updating to a new version
docs.text:
What carries over: your config.json settings (theme color, rules, team, social headers and everything else) and your own images, audio and videos in html/assets/.

To update:

  1. Back up html/config.json and any files you added under html/assets/.
  2. Replace the resource: delete the old 4zam_loading folder and extract the new release in its place.
  3. Put your files back: copy your config.json over the new one and your files back into html/assets/.
  4. Restart the server.

Or skip the copying: import your old config.json into the Config Builder and export a fresh resource, which always uses the latest version.

Check the Changelog for what changed. New options are optional, so an older config.json keeps working.

Before you update

  • Do not overwrite your config.json unless the release notes explicitly say to.
  • If you changed the loading screen's own styles or code, back them up first: an update replaces them.

Coming from gucci_loading?

The resource was renamed to 4zam_loading in v1.2.0. Rename your folder to 4zam_loading and change your server.cfg line to ensure 4zam_loading.

docs.title: 🧷 Social Header Configuration
docs.text:
You can customize the social header cards that appear at the top of the loading screen. These cards allow users to quickly join your Discord, visit your Instagram or check out other platforms.

Quicker in the Config Builder

The Config Builder sets all of this under Social Links with a live preview, and Build with AI can set it up from a plain description. Every field with its type and default is in the Config reference: socialHeaders.

docs.title: JSON Structure
docs.text:
"socialHeaders": [
    { 
        "type": "discord", 
        "cardLabel": "Discord Server", 
        "cardInfo": "Join the discord to keep up with the latest on the FiveM server!", 
        "link": "https://discord.gg/dbFChqBh5u", 
        "buttonLabel": "Join",
        "enabled": true 
    }
]

docs.title: Field Breakdown
docs.text:
Each card takes type, cardLabel, cardInfo, link, buttonLabel and enabled: types and details are in the Config reference. The link opens when the card button is clicked. Leave buttonLabel empty to use the default "Join" text.

Multiple Platforms Supported

You can include multiple social cards by adding more objects to the socialHeaders array.

docs.title: Supported type values
docs.text:
The built-in platforms plus custom (your own icon) are listed under socialHeaders[].type in the Config reference.

Spelling Matters

The type value must be lowercase and spelled exactly as listed in the Config reference to display the correct icon.

Social Media Card Preview

docs.title: Custom Icon Support
docs.text: You can use your own icon instead of the built-in ones by setting type to "custom" and providing an image path in the config.

docs.title: Example: Tebex / Store Icon
docs.text:
"socialHeaders": [
    {
        "type": "discord",
        "cardLabel": "Discord Server",
        "cardInfo": "Join the discord to keep up with the latest on the FiveM server!",
        "link": "https://discord.gg/dbFChqBh5u",
        "buttonLabel": "Join",
        "enabled": true
    },
    {
        "type": "custom",
        "cardLabel": "Tebex Store",
        "cardInfo": "Purchase perks and content through our Tebex store!",
        "link": "https://your-tebex-link-here",
        "buttonLabel": "Shop Now",
        "enabled": true,

        "imagePath": "./assets/jpg/tebex.jpg",
        "imageWidth": "3vw",
        "imageHeight": "3vh"
    }
]

docs.title: Custom Icon Fields
docs.text:
• imagePath: your icon image, a URL or a path inside the resource. Needed for custom.
  • imageWidth and imageHeight: optional, any valid CSS size (px, vw, vh, % and so on).

Types are in the Config reference.

docs.title: Why imageWidth and imageHeight are exposed
docs.text:
Different icons will have different aspect ratios and visual weight. Since this script cannot guarantee that every custom image will automatically fit perfectly inside the button, you, the server owner, have full control over the icon size:

  • Use imageWidth and imageHeight to tweak how big the icon appears in the button
  • If omitted, a default size will be used, but this might not look ideal for all assets
  • This lets you adjust per-icon without editing the code
Custom Tebex Icon Example Preview

docs.title: Recommended Icon Formats
docs.text:
For best results:

  • SVG (preferred)

    • Sharp at any size
    • Perfect for logos
    • Small file size

  • PNG (transparent background preferred)

    • At least 256×256 or 512×512
    • Great for icons with soft edges or glow effects
    • Preserves transparency for cleaner UI visuals

  • JPEG / JPG (supported but not ideal)

    • Works fine if your image does not require transparency
    • Useful for rectangular logos or photos
    • Should be high resolution to avoid blurring

Avoid

  • Low-resolution PNG/JPEG images
  • Icons with solid white/black background when transparency is needed
  • Very wide or tall aspect-ratios that distort inside the social buttons

docs.title: 👥 Team Panel Configuration
docs.text:
The Team Panel appears on the right-hand side of the loading screen and showcases your server staff or contributors.

You can fully customize each member by editing the teamMembers array in your configuration file.

Quicker in the Config Builder

The Config Builder sets all of this under Team with a live preview, and Build with AI can set it up from a plain description. Every field with its type and default is in the Config reference: teamMembers.

docs.title: JSON Structure
docs.text:
"teamMembers": [
    { "name": "GucciFlipFlops", "role": "Head Developer", "discord": "pakinextdoor", "image": "./assets/png/fakalheadshot.png" }
]

docs.title: Field Breakdown
docs.text:
Each member takes name (shown prominently), role (a smaller line under it), discord (usually a Discord username, but any short label works) and image (shown in a circle, so a square 1:1 picture looks best). Types are in the Config reference.

Adding More Members

To add more team members, simply add more objects inside the teamMembers array.

Team Panel Preview

docs.title: ✨ Title Animation
docs.text:
Control how the watermark title (your server name) animates, and toggle the sweeping sheen highlight over it.

These options live inside watermark.label, right alongside the title text.

Quicker in the Config Builder

The Config Builder sets all of this under Brand & Color with a live preview, and Build with AI can set it up from a plain description. Every field with its type and default is in the Config reference: watermark.

docs.title: JSON Structure
docs.text:
"watermark": {
  "label": {
    "text": "The Vibe RP",
    "colorWordCount": 2,
    "animation": "wave",
    "sheen": true
  }
}

docs.title: Field Breakdown
docs.text:
label.animation picks the preset and label.sheen turns the sweeping light on or off (true by default). Both are in the Config reference.

Defaults

If animation is missing or set to a value that doesn't exist, the title falls back to wave. If sheen is omitted, the sheen is on: set "sheen": false to turn it off.

docs.title: Available Presets
docs.text:
Every preset is hand-tuned to look premium and animates smoothly without straining the FiveM UI. The full list, with what each preset looks like, is generated from the code: see title animation presets.

Sheen layers on top

sheen is independent of animation. The sheen sweep runs over whichever preset you pick, so you can pair, for example, wave + sheen or slam + sheen.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
A calm, premium look:

"label": { "text": "The Vibe RP", "colorWordCount": 2, "animation": "sway", "sheen": true }

A high-energy, beat-driven look:

"label": { "text": "The Vibe RP", "colorWordCount": 2, "animation": "pulse", "sheen": true }

A completely static title with no sheen:

"label": { "text": "The Vibe RP", "colorWordCount": 2, "animation": "none", "sheen": false }

Where the title comes from

text and colorWordCount (the title itself and its color split) are documented on the Watermark page. animation and sheen only control how that text moves and shines.

docs.title: Troubleshooting & FAQ
docs.text: Most problems are fixed fastest in the Config Builder: import your config.json, check the live preview and export again. The Build with AI page also has a support assistant you can ask in plain words.

docs.title: YouTube backgrounds
docs.text:
YouTube links work as backgrounds. Since v1.3.0 they play in game through a small player page hosted at loadingscreen.4zam.dev, with sound, pause and volume working as usual. Paste a normal video link; no setup is needed.

Why this was needed

FiveM loads loading screens from nui://, which sends no Referer, so YouTube used to reject every embed with "Error 153: video player configuration error". The hosted player page fixes that.

docs.title: If a YouTube video will not play
docs.text:
The video owner's settings still apply. Check the video in YouTube Studio > Content and make sure it has:

  • Embedding allowed (Video > Settings > Permissions > "Allow embedding")
  • No age restriction
  • No region or copyright blocks
  • Public or unlisted visibility

Also:

  • Use a link to one video. Playlist and channel links are not supported as backgrounds. A video link that carries playlist details (&list=...) plays just that video.
  • The player page needs loadingscreen.4zam.dev to be reachable from the player's PC.

When a video cannot play, the screen moves on to your next video or to your music within about 15 seconds. If every video fails, it shows a short notice and falls back to your background image, so the screen never sits black.

Most reliable: a local file

If a video still refuses to play, download it and use a local .webm or .mp4 file instead. Local files never depend on YouTube or on our player page.

docs.title: Video tips
docs.text:
• Local files are fastest. Put the file in html/assets/ and point to it as ./assets/background.webm. .webm is the safest format for FiveM.
  • Keep files small. A short, compressed loop loads faster for every player than a long high-bitrate video.
  • A video beats an image. When both are set, the video plays and the image is the fallback.
  • Video or music for sound? videoAsAudio: true makes the video the audio source. false plays it muted on loop while your music playlist plays. Left out, the video is the audio only when you have no music. See videoAsAudio.
  • Several videos: give backgroundVideo a list and players can skip between them. See backgroundVideo.

docs.title: The loading screen does not show
docs.text:
• The folder must be named exactly 4zam_loading and your server.cfg must have ensure 4zam_loading.
  • Only one loading screen can run. Stop any other resource that declares a loadscreen.
  • Restart the server after adding it, then reconnect.

docs.title: The loading screen does not close after spawning
docs.text: The resource keeps the screen up until your game mode closes it (loadscreen_manual_shutdown 'yes' in fxmanifest.lua). Most frameworks close it automatically on spawn. If yours does not, remove that line from fxmanifest.lua and restart.

docs.title: My changes do not show up
docs.text:
• Restart the resource (restart 4zam_loading) or the server, then reconnect.
  • Make sure config.json is still valid JSON: one missing comma breaks the whole file. Importing it into the Config Builder shows whether it reads correctly.

docs.title: An image, video or song does not load
docs.text:
• Local files go in html/assets/ and are written as ./assets/your-file.png.
  • Check the exact file name, including capital letters. Avoid spaces in file names.
  • For links, use a direct https:// link to the file itself, not to a page that shows it.

docs.title: The music player is missing
docs.text: The player hides when there is nothing to play: add at least one track to music, or use a video as the audio source.

docs.title: Text in Arabic or Urdu
docs.text: Set language to ar or ur and the screen's text renders right to left, with a bundled font. Your own text (rules, names, panel entries) is shown as you wrote it. See language.

docs.title: FAQ
docs.text:
Is it free? Yes. The resource and the Config Builder are free.

Does it work with my framework? Yes. It is a standalone loading screen, so it works with any framework.

Can I use my own images, videos and music? Yes. Upload them in the builder and they are bundled into your download, or put them in html/assets/ yourself.

Where are all the options listed? In the Config reference.

Still stuck? Ask the support assistant on Build with AI, or reach the community on the community hub.

docs.title: 🏷️ Watermark Configuration
docs.text:
Customize the watermark that appears in the top-left corner of the loading screen.

Quicker in the Config Builder

The Config Builder sets all of this under Brand & Color with a live preview, and Build with AI can set it up from a plain description. Every field with its type and default is in the Config reference: watermark.

docs.title: JSON Structure
docs.text:
"watermark": { 
    "label": { "text": "The Vibe RP", "colorWordCount": 2, "animation": "wave", "sheen": true }, 
    "subHeading": "Loading Screen", 
    "logo": "./assets/png/logo.png" 
}

docs.title: Field Breakdown
docs.text:
Every field (label.text, label.colorWordCount, label.animation, label.sheen, subHeading, logo) with its type and default is in the Config reference. The logo can be a URL or a path inside the resource such as ./assets/png/logo.png.

Animating the title

label.animation and label.sheen control how the title moves and shines. See the Title Animation page for the full preset list.

Color Tip

The colorWordCount applies the highlight color to that number of starting words in the label.text.

Watermark Preview
